Acceleration.description: How the speed of a movement changes how far the pointer goes.

oneOf.description:
A quick movement takes the pointer further than a slow one of the
same length: slow for precision, quick to cross the screen.
The pointer goes as far as the device moved, however quickly.

Align.description: Where along the edge two screens share one is lined up with the other.

oneOf.description: Their tops, or their left sides, in line.
Their middles in line.
Their bottoms, or their right sides, in line.

enabled.description:
Whether what is copied is kept by `omorfos-clipboard` once the
program it was copied from has closed. Turn it off to have another
program keep it, or none. What a password manager copies is never
kept.

Color.description: A colour as `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` with its opacity.

Command.description: A program followed by its arguments, run without a shell.

Cursor.description: The pictures used for the pointer.

size.description: The size of the pointer, before scaling.

theme.description:
The name of an installed cursor theme, such as `Adwaita`. `default`
is whichever the system has set up as its default.

Fit.description: How a picture is laid on a screen.

oneOf.description:
As large as it must be to cover the screen, its shape kept, and
what does not fit cut off on two sides.

As large as fits on the screen, its shape kept, with the colour
round it.
Made the screen's size and shape.
As it is, a pixel of it to a pixel of the screen, in the middle.
As it is, again and again from the top left corner.

raise_on_focus.description: Whether focusing a window also raises it above the others.

oneOf.description: A window is focused when it is clicked.

A window is focused when the pointer enters it, and keeps focus while
the pointer is over the desktop.

Idle.description: What happens when the user is away.

screen_off.description:
Seconds without input after which the screens are turned off. `0`
never turns them off.

Kept.description: Where a picture of the screen goes.

oneOf.description: Saved as a file among the user's pictures.
Copied, to be pasted, and not saved.
Saved and copied.

layout.description: XKB layout, such as `us` or `gb,pl` for several.

repeat_delay.description: Milliseconds a key is held before it starts repeating.

repeat_rate.description: Repeats per second once repeating starts. `0` disables key repeat.

variant.description: XKB variant, such as `dvorak`. Empty for the default.

Launcher.description:
The launcher that comes with omorfos: what it shows of each program
besides its name.

descriptions.description:
Whether what each program says of itself is shown after its name,
and looked through for what is typed.

icons.description: Whether each program's icon is shown beside its name.

Lock.description:
How the lock screen that comes with omorfos may be unlocked, and what
else it offers. The password always may unlock, so that a reader that
fails never keeps the user out; each other way is offered beside it
where PAM is set up for it, and whichever is shown first unlocks.

fingerprint.description:
A finger on the reader, through the `omorfos-lock-fingerprint` PAM
service.

key.description:
A security key touched, such as a `YubiKey`, through the
`omorfos-lock-key` PAM service.

power.description:
Sleep, Restart, Shut Down and Log Out, without unlocking, each
where it may be done without a password. Whoever is at the screen
can then end the session, and what is not saved in it; a machine
that others use may want them off.

Mouse.description:
Mouse behaviour. A mouse and a touchpad are set apart because people
expect opposite things of them.

acceleration.description:
Whether a quick movement takes the pointer further than a slow one
of the same length.

natural_scroll.description:
Whether content follows the wheel when scrolling. A wheel turned
towards the user moves down the page unless this is on.

speed.description: How fast the pointer moves with the mouse.

NamedOutput.description: One screen, by the name of the socket it is plugged into.

align.description:
Where along the edge it shares with the one before it it is lined
up: at the start, the top or the left; the middle; or the end.
Without this, the start beside it, and the middle above or below.

enabled.description:
Whether it is on. One that is not shows nothing and stands nowhere,
unless every screen plugged in would be off, when it is left on.

mirror.description:
Another screen, by name, whose picture this one shows, as large as
fits on it: it stands nowhere of its own, and has nothing of its
own on it. Without that one plugged in, it is a screen like any.

mode.description:
The size it is driven at, and how often it is drawn. Without this,
what the screen says suits it best.

name.description:
The screen's name, such as `eDP-1` or `HDMI-A-1`, as `omorfosctl
state` shows it.

offset.description:
How far along that edge it is moved from there: right or down, or
left or up if less than nothing.

place.description:
Where it stands next to the screen listed before it: to its right,
unless this says otherwise.

primary.description:
Whether it is the one that comes first: the one the notice of what
is wrong is shown on, and that windows go to from a screen that is
unplugged. Without one, the first screen plugged in. One screen at
most.

rotate.description:
Which way the screen is turned, as `xrandr --rotate` says it: what
is drawn is turned to match, so that it stands the right way up.

scale.description:
How large everything is drawn on it. Without this, the scale given
for every screen applies.

Notifications.description:
The notifications that come with omorfos: what programs have to tell
the user, shown in a corner of the screen.

enabled.description:
Whether they are shown by omorfos. Turn it off to go without, or
to use another program for them.

timeout.description:
How long one stays, in seconds, when the program that sent it does
not say. `0` leaves it until it is clicked.

oneOf.description: Units of layout, less than nothing for left or up.
A share of the screen's own length, such as `-30%`.

Order.description: The order the pictures of a directory are shown in.

oneOf.description: By their names.
Any order, a different one each time through.

scale.description:
How large everything is drawn: `auto` to suit the screen, or a
number from 1 to 4 in steps of 0.25.

oneOf.description: Whatever suits the screen.
Pixels to a unit of layout.

Outputs.description: Screens by name, in the order they stand from the left.

Panel.description:
The panel that comes with omorfos: a bar along the bottom of each
screen.

enabled.description:
Whether it is started with the session. Turn it off to go without
a panel or to use another one.

Picture.description: A path from the root, or from the home directory as `~/`.

Place.description: Where a screen stands next to the one listed before it.

oneOf.description: To its right, the tops in line.
To its left, the tops in line.
Above it, the middles in line.
Below it, the middles in line.

Placement.description: Where a new window appears when no rule positions it.

oneOf.description: Each window is offset from the previous one, so titlebars stay visible.
In the middle of the screen.
Under the pointer.

Portals.description:
What applications ask the desktop through the portals
(`xdg-desktop-portal`), such as whether it is light or dark.

enabled.description:
Whether omorfos answers them. Turn it off to have another
program answer, or none.

Role.description:
Something a program may do only if the compositor started it and was
told it may.

oneOf.description:
Put surfaces on the screen outside windows and keep room for them,
and list the windows.
Cover the screen and take the keyboard while it does.
Lock the session.
Show the prompt that asks for a secret.
Take pictures of the screen and of windows.
Read and set the clipboard at any time.
Type and click as the user, and see what is typed into fields.
Arrange the screens and change their colour.

Rotation.description:
Which way a screen is turned, with the top of what it shows: where it
is as made, on the left, on the right, or at the bottom.

oneOf.description: As it was made.
A quarter turn to the left: the top of the picture on the left.
A quarter turn to the right: the top of the picture on the right.
Upside down.

ScreenMode.description: The size in pixels, such as `2560x1440`, and how many times a second it is drawn if that matters, such as `2560x1440@144`.

ScreenWallpaper.description: What one screen shows, by the name of the socket it is plugged into.

fit.description: Its own way of laying the picture on it.

name.description:
The screen's name, such as `eDP-1` or `HDMI-A-1`, as `omorfosctl
state` shows it.

picture.description:
Its own picture, or directory of them. With this or `color`, it
shows nothing of what every screen does.

Screens.description: Screens by name, each named once.

Screenshots.description: Pictures of the screen, as `omorfos-screenshot` takes them.

destination.description: Where a picture goes when the program is not told otherwise.

Speed.description: From -1, the slowest, to 1, the fastest; 0 is what the device is made for.

Started.description: A program to start with the session: its name and arguments, or that and what it may do.

may.description: What it may do that an ordinary program may not.

acceleration.description:
Whether a quick movement takes the pointer further than a slow one
of the same length.

natural_scroll.description: Whether content follows the fingers when scrolling.

speed.description: How fast the pointer moves under a finger.

Wallpaper.description:
The wallpaper that comes with omorfos: a picture or a colour on each
screen, behind everything else.

Without a picture or a colour the theme's `desktop` part is all there
is behind the windows.

color.description:
The colour of the screen where the picture does not cover it, or of
the whole screen without one. Without this, the background of the
theme's `desktop` part.

enabled.description:
Whether it is started with the session. Turn it off to use another
program for it.

every.description: How many seconds each picture of a directory is shown for.

fade.description:
How many milliseconds what a screen shows takes to fade into what
it shows next. 0 is at once.

fit.description: How the picture is laid on the screen.

order.description: The order the pictures of a directory are shown in.

picture.description:
A picture, PNG or JPEG, or a directory of them to be shown in turn:
a path from the root, or from the home directory as `~/`.

screens.description: Particular screens, by name, that show something else.

X11Scaling.description:
How programs written for X11 are drawn on a screen with a scale. X11
has no notion of one, so something has to give.

oneOf.description:
They draw at one pixel to a unit of layout and are stretched to
size. All of them are the right size, and blurred.

Xwayland.description: Programs written for X11, which run through `Xwayland`.

enabled.description:
Whether `Xwayland` is started with the session. Turn it off to do
without programs written for X11: they can read each other's
windows and keys, which programs written for Wayland cannot.

scaling.description: How they are drawn on a screen with a scale.

arrangements.description:
Screens as `outputs` lists them, for when just those are plugged
in: the first that names exactly the screens there are is used in
place of `outputs`.

autostart.description:
Programs to start with the session, each as a program and its
arguments, or as that and what it may do. They are started once, in
order, and not again when the configuration is reloaded.

idle.description: What happens when the user is away.

launcher.description: The launcher that comes with omorfos.

lock.description:
How `omorfos-lock` may be unlocked, besides the password, and what
else it offers.

locker.description:
The program that locks the session, and its arguments, such as
`[swaylock, -f]`. The `lock` action starts it, and it alone is let
lock. Without one there is nothing to lock with.

notifications.description: The notifications that come with omorfos.

output.description: How every screen is driven, unless it is named in `outputs`.

outputs.description:
Particular screens, by name: where each stands and how it is
driven.

panel.description: The panel that comes with omorfos.

portals.description: What applications ask the desktop through the portals.

wallpaper.description: What is shown behind the windows.

workspaces.description: The workspaces of the session, as a list of names.
